title: Exploratory pilot study to investigate the subjective assessment of sound improvement by an AI algorithm trained using self-fitting
summary:
This exploratory study examines how people aged 55 and older with age-related hearing loss evaluate a new AI algorithm (AIHearS) on a smartphone. This algorithm is designed to help improve sound quality and make speech easier to understand. The study tests an initial version of the software, which is still under development. The study focuses in particular on how the AI algorithm “learns” and adapts through use.

The study is part of the “AI Hearing System” project funded by the BMBF. The aim of the study is to further develop the AI algorithm and find out how users accept and use the technology.
conditions: Mild to moderate symmetrical age-related hearing loss

interventions.name: App-supported training of an AI algorithm via self-fitting of sound preferences in standardized sound situations for older adults with previous experience in using hearing aids
App-supported training of an AI algorithm via self-fitting of sound preferences in standardized sound situations for older adults without previous experience in using hearing aids

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
− Mild to moderate age-related hearing loss (declining hearing loss, hearing curve N2 and N4, assessed as part of the study)
− Age: 55 years and older
− German-speaking: able to understand German-language texts and instructions
− People with and without hearing aids (recorded via questionnaire)
Exclusion criteria:
− Asymmetric hearing loss
− Legal guardianship
− Cognitive impairments (self-reported)
− Tinnitus (cause of hearing loss, uncompensated tinnitus)
− Visual impairments that hinder the use of smartphones
− Hand impairments that hinder the use of smartphones
